name: Kristian Birkeland
summary: Norwegian physicist and pioneer of space plasma physics known for explaining auroras and geomagnetic disturbances.

name: A. Egeland
summary: Co-author of the source document and historian of science at the University of Oslo.

name: W. J. Burke
summary: Co-author of the source document and scientist at the Air Force Research Laboratory.

name: Oslo
summary: Capital city of Norway, formerly named Kristiania.

name: Tokyo
summary: Capital city of Japan where Birkeland died.

name: Norway
summary: Scandinavian country where Birkeland was born and conducted most of his work.

name: University of Oslo
summary: Norwegian university where Birkeland was appointed professor of physics.

name: Norsk Hydro
summary: Norwegian industrial enterprise founded partly through Birkeland's nitrogen fixation method.

name: Terrella
summary: Laboratory simulation device invented by Birkeland to model cosmic phenomena.

name: The Norwegian Aurora Polaris Expedition 1902–1903
summary: Birkeland's 801-page monograph summarizing his main work on auroras and geomagnetic disturbances.

name: Sydney Chapman
summary: British mathematician and scientist who criticized Birkeland's field-aligned current conjecture.

name: Hannes Alfvén
summary: Swedish physicist and Nobel Laureate who championed Birkeland's work on field-aligned currents.

name: Elisar Boye
summary: Birkeland's student assistant who died in an avalanche during the 1899–1900 expedition.

name: International Union for Geomagnetism and Aeronomy
summary: Scientific union that ratified the name 'Birkeland currents' for field-aligned currents.

name: TRIAD satellite
summary: Satellite that provided the first direct measurements of field-aligned currents in 1966.

name: Finnmark
summary: Norway's northernmost province where Birkeland conducted auroral expeditions.

name: Haldde Mountain
summary: Location of a permanent observatory built for Birkeland's 1899–1900 expedition.

name: French Academy
summary: Academy where Birkeland published 32 of his 88 scientific papers.

name: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
summary: Academy that cooperated to inaugurate The Kristian Birkeland Lectures.

name: Norwegian 200-kroner banknote
summary: Banknote issued in 1994 featuring Birkeland's portrait and terrella experiment.

name: The Kristian Birkeland Lectures
summary: Continuing lecture series inaugurated in 1986 to commemorate Birkeland's achievements.

name: Birkeland-Eyde method
summary: Industrial nitrogen fixation method invented by Birkeland using a plasma arc.
